text: The tensor unit is the base semiring R with trivial right coaction r↦r⊗1. The bialgebra laws make 1 group-like, so this is a comodule, and R is generated by 1 over itself. It supplies the usual unit for the [comodule tensor product in EGNO §1.21](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=44). Checks pass: [trivial_coact_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Trivial.lean#L225), [leftUnitor_hom_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/Monoidal.lean#L213).
Evaluates the explicitly selected trivial coaction.
Tensoring this unit on the left recovers scalar multiplication.

Reassociation sends (m⊗n)⊗p to m⊗(n⊗p), without permuting factors. It respects the diagonal coaction because (cd)e=c(de) in the coefficient bialgebra, matching [EGNO’s tensor comodule construction](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=44). The linear equivalence then gives the inverse comodule map automatically; no commutativity of coefficients is required. Checks pass: [associator_hom_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/Monoidal.lean#L233), [associator_inv_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/Monoidal.lean#L239).
Checks forward reassociation on pure tensors.
Checks the actual inverse reassociation.

The left unit map R⊗M→M is r⊗m↦rm, with inverse m↦1⊗m, as in the [tensor unit isomorphism, Stacks 10.12.3](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00CV). It intertwines the coactions because the unit comodule contributes coefficient 1 and 1c=c. The source packages this genuine linear equivalence as a comodule isomorphism. Checks pass: [leftUnitor_hom_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/Monoidal.lean#L213), [leftUnitor_inv_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/Monoidal.lean#L218).
Evaluates the forward map as scalar multiplication.
Evaluates its inverse as insertion of 1 on the left.

The right unit map M⊗R→M sends m⊗r to rm and has inverse m↦m⊗1. These are the usual [tensor unit identifications](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00CV). Coaction compatibility uses c1=c, so the coefficient bialgebra need not commute; the source supplies both inverse maps from the ordinary tensor linear equivalence. Checks pass: [rightUnitor_hom_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/Monoidal.lean#L223), [rightUnitor_inv_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/Monoidal.lean#L228).
Evaluates the forward map as scalar multiplication.
Evaluates the inverse as insertion of 1 on the right.

This packages the diagonal tensor product, trivial unit, reassociation, and left/right unit maps as the operations underlying a monoidal category. They are the standard [comodule tensor operations in EGNO §1.21](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=44). This declaration supplies the data; the separate monoidal-category instance verifies their coherence. Finite means finitely generated as a module. Checks pass: [tensorHom_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/Monoidal.lean#L206), [tensorAssociator_eq](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/Monoidal.lean#L182).
Tensor products of categorical morphisms act componentwise.
Identifies the chosen associator with the monoidal notation.

The finite comodules form a monoidal category with diagonal tensor product, as over fields in [EGNO §1.21](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=44). The source proves coherence by the faithful forgetful functor: reassociation and unit maps become the ordinary semimodule maps, whose triangle and pentagon identities hold. A general bialgebra suffices; symmetry and rigidity are not asserted. Checks pass: [associator_inv_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/Monoidal.lean#L239), [leftUnitor_hom_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/Monoidal.lean#L213), [rightUnitor_hom_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/Monoidal.lean#L223).
Checks the concrete inverse associator of this structure.
Checks its left unit comparison.
Checks its right unit comparison.

The inverse left unit map inserts the scalar 1: m↦1⊗m. Applying the forward map gives 1·m=m; conversely, tensor balancing recovers r⊗m from rm. Thus the formula is the standard [tensor unit inverse](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00CV), on the actual finite-comodule isomorphism, with no choice of basis or finite generating set. Checks pass: [leftUnitor_hom_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/Monoidal.lean#L213), [leftUnitor_inv_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/Monoidal.lean#L271).
The forward unit map is scalar multiplication.
Identifies the inverse with the ordinary tensor linear equivalence.

The inverse right unit map inserts 1 in the second factor: m↦m⊗1. Scalar multiplication is its inverse by tensor balancing, in accord with the [tensor unit isomorphisms](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00CV). The factors are not exchanged; the source evaluates precisely the inverse of the selected right comodule unitor. Checks pass: [rightUnitor_hom_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/Monoidal.lean#L223), [rightUnitor_inv_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/Monoidal.lean#L287).
The forward right unit map is scalar multiplication.
Identifies the underlying inverse linear map.

The associator changes brackets only: (m⊗n)⊗p becomes m⊗(n⊗p). This matches [Stacks 10.12.5](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00CV); no permutation or sign appears. The source uses the ordinary tensor associativity equivalence, already proved coaction-compatible using associativity of coefficient multiplication, so the equation also describes the finite-comodule morphism. Checks pass: [associator_inv_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/Monoidal.lean#L239), [associator_hom_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/Monoidal.lean#L247).
The inverse restores the original bracketing.
Identifies the full linear map with the standard associator.

After forgetting coactions, the categorical associator is exactly the ordinary linear map (M⊗N)⊗P→M⊗(N⊗P). Equality is checked on pure triple tensors, which generate the source. This is the [associativity isomorphism of Stacks 10.12.5](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00CV), not merely an unspecified equivalence between modules of equal dimension. Checks pass: [associator_hom_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/Monoidal.lean#L233), [associator_inv_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/Monoidal.lean#L255).
Checks the generating pure triple tensors.
Identifies the inverse linear map with inverse reassociation.

Forgetting the coaction sends the inverse left unitor to the linear map m↦1⊗m. The source proves equality elementwise from its concrete inverse formula, so the chosen categorical isomorphism has the expected [tensor unit inverse](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00CV). This is an identity of linear maps, without a basis or dimension argument. Checks pass: [leftUnitor_inv_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/Monoidal.lean#L218), [leftUnitor_hom_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/Monoidal.lean#L263).
Provides the elementwise inverse formula.
Identifies the corresponding forward tensor identity.

The inverse right unitor has underlying linear map m↦m⊗1, the inverse of scalar multiplication M⊗R→M. This agrees with the [ordinary tensor unit identifications](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00CV). The proof compares values on every module element and therefore identifies the actual map, including its tensor-factor order, over a commutative semiring. Checks pass: [rightUnitor_inv_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/Monoidal.lean#L228), [rightUnitor_hom_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/Monoidal.lean#L279).
Provides the elementwise inverse formula.
Identifies its forward linear inverse.

Scalar extension preserves tensor products through (a⊗m)⊗(b⊗n)↦ab⊗(m⊗n), and the unit through a↦a⊗1. Both maps are invertible, giving a strong monoidal functor in the sense of [EGNO §1.4](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=14). The source checks associativity and unit coherence on generating tensors; the value algebra A is commutative. Checks pass: [scalarExtensionFunctor_μ](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/ScalarExtension/Monoidal.lean#L196), [scalarExtensionFunctor_δ](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/ScalarExtension/Monoidal.lean#L212), [scalarExtensionFunctor_ε](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/ScalarExtension/Monoidal.lean#L205).
Identifies the tensor comparison.
Identifies its inverse.
Identifies the unit comparison.

This bundles scalar extension with its tensor and unit comparison maps. The output type retains the lax structure, although the source has proved both comparisons invertible. In [EGNO §1.4](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=14), these are the extra data required of a monoidal functor; the underlying assignment remains M↦A⊗_R M. Checks pass: [scalarExtensionMonoidalFunctor_toFunctor](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/ScalarExtension/Monoidal.lean#L190), [scalarExtensionFunctor_μ](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/ScalarExtension/Monoidal.lean#L196).
The underlying functor is unchanged scalar extension.
Checks its inherited tensor comparison.

The tensor comparison combines scalar factors: (a⊗m)⊗_A(b⊗n)↦ab⊗(m⊗n). It is inverse to distributing scalar extension across a tensor product, with only equality identifications around the map. This has the [monoidal comparison direction of EGNO §1.4](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=14); commutativity of A makes the displayed A-balanced operation valid. Checks pass: [scalarExtensionFunctor_δ](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/ScalarExtension/Monoidal.lean#L212), [scalarExtensionMonoidalFunctor_toFunctor](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/ScalarExtension/Monoidal.lean#L190).
The inverse comparison distributes a scalar-extended tensor.
The comparison belongs to the stated scalar-extension functor.

The unit comparison goes from the target unit A to the scalar extension A⊗_R R of the source unit, by a↦a⊗1. Its inverse is a⊗r↦a·algebraMap(r). Thus it has the direction required by [EGNO’s unit comparison](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=14); equality transports only align the bundled objects. Checks pass: [scalarExtensionFunctor_η](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/ScalarExtension/Monoidal.lean#L221), [scalarExtensionMonoidalFunctor_toFunctor](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/ScalarExtension/Monoidal.lean#L190).
Identifies the inverse unit comparison.
Confirms the underlying functor whose units are compared.

An algebra-valued point g acts on A⊗M by evaluating the coefficient leg of the right coaction. Comodule morphisms intertwine these actions, giving naturality as in [Milne §9a, condition(c)](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=175). The inverse point gives inverse components. The source proves this for arbitrary comodules over a Hopf algebra over a commutative semiring, beyond the reference’s field setting. Checks pass: [baseChange_comp_endOfPoint](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/PointsAction.lean#L164), [pointNatIso_inv_app](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/ScalarExtension.lean#L116).
Comodule maps intertwine the scalar-extended point actions.
The inverse component is the inverse point-action map.

The component at M is the point action on A⊗M, with equality maps identifying the functor’s bundled value. Concretely, a⊗m goes to Σa·g(m₁)⊗m₀. This realizes the natural family considered in [Milne §9a](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=175); the source’s right-coaction convention determines the coefficient evaluation and factor order. Checks pass: [endOfPoint_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/PointsAction.lean#L119), [pointNatIso_inv_app](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/ScalarExtension.lean#L116).
Evaluates the point action on a simple tensor.
Checks the inverse component uses the same object identifications.

Points act on the scalar-extension functor by a group homomorphism: convolution g*h acts as g after h, and the counit point acts identically. These are the action laws underlying [Milne’s natural point family](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=175). The proof checks components; categorical Aut multiplication uses exactly this order. No reconstruction or injectivity is claimed. Checks pass: [endOfPoint_convMul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/PointsAction.lean#L426), [endOfPoint_convOne](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/PointsAction.lean#L370).
Convolution product acts as ordered composition.
The counit point gives the identity action.

Restricting the all-comodule point action to finitely generated comodules preserves its group law, by precomposing natural transformations with the inclusion. The functor’s defining equality only identifies this restriction with finite scalar extension. This supplies the finite natural family of [Milne §9a](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=175), without asserting that every natural automorphism arises from a point. Checks pass: [fgPointNatIsoHom_hom_app](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/ScalarExtension.lean#L188), [fgPointNatIsoHom_inv_app](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/ScalarExtension.lean#L207).
The restricted forward component is the original point action.
The restricted inverse component is the original inverse action.

The finite-comodule component is the same linear point action on A⊗M as before restriction. The proof cancels the identifications introduced by precomposition and the defining functor equality. This matches the finite natural family in [Milne §9a](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=175); finite generation changes the range of objects tested, not the formula on elements. Checks pass: [pointNatIso_hom_app](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/ScalarExtension.lean#L106), [fgPointNatIsoHom_inv_app](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/ScalarExtension.lean#L207).
Identifies the ambient component before restriction.
Checks the inverse component after the same restriction.

Given a natural isomorphism i:F≅G, tensor comparison for G first moves both inputs through i⁻¹, uses F’s comparison, then applies i; the unit comparison similarly ends with i. Cancelling inverse pairs transfers the [lax coherence diagrams of Tate, p.2](https://www.cs.cornell.edu/courses/cs6117/2020sp/lectures/Monoidal.pdf#page=2). The comparisons themselves need not be invertible. Checks pass: [transport_μ](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Functor.lean#L219), [transport_ε](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Functor.lean#L213).
Checks the transferred tensor comparison in its exact direction.
Checks the transferred unit comparison.

The transported tensor map G(X)⊗G(Y)→G(X⊗Y) is i_(X⊗Y)∘μ_F∘(i_X⁻¹⊗i_Y⁻¹). Its direction matches the [lax tensor comparison in Tate, p.2](https://www.cs.cornell.edu/courses/cs6117/2020sp/lectures/Monoidal.pdf#page=2). The local structure hypothesis explicitly selects this transported structure on G; the formula does not describe an arbitrary independently chosen lax structure. Checks pass: [transport_μ_assoc](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Functor.lean#L220).
The exported reassociated form verifies the same formula after arbitrary postcomposition.

The transported unit map starts at the target tensor unit, applies F’s unit comparison, then i at the source tensor unit. This is the direction in the [lax unit diagram of Tate, p.2](https://www.cs.cornell.edu/courses/cs6117/2020sp/lectures/Monoidal.pdf#page=2). The source unfolds the specifically transported structure; it neither reverses i nor assumes the unit comparison invertible. Checks pass: [transport_ε_assoc](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Functor.lean#L214).
The exported reassociated formula verifies compatibility with arbitrary postcomposition.

Over a commutative ring, additive inverses on the underlying semimodule are supplied by −m=(−1)·m. The module laws prove cancellation. The source directly reuses [Mathlib’s construction](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Module/NatInt.lean#L90), preserving addition and scalar multiplication; the ring hypothesis is essential here, whereas the earlier finite-comodule category allows semirings. Checks pass: [forget₂_semimoduleCat_obj](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/Basic.lean#L136).
Forgetting exposes the same underlying additive module, now specialized to a ring.

A Hölder triple records the exponent relation 1/p+1/q=1/r for extended nonnegative exponents. It packages that equation, rather than an inequality about functions. For positive finite r, dividing p and q by r gives conjugate exponents. The definition also admits zero-exponent cases through the convention 0⁻¹=∞; these are extensions of the arithmetic relation. Compared with [Faris §23.7](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Holder.lean#L42).

Two extended nonnegative exponents are Hölder conjugate when their reciprocals sum to one. This is the triple relation with output exponent one. It includes the familiar pair (2,2) and the endpoint pairs (1,∞) and (∞,1), using ∞⁻¹=0. The equation forces each exponent to be at least one, so zero is excluded. Compared with [Faris §23.7](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Holder.lean#L46).

For any extended nonnegative p and q, choosing r=(p⁻¹+q⁻¹)⁻¹ produces a Hölder triple. Reciprocal is involutive even at zero and infinity, so no positivity or finiteness assumptions are needed for this algebraic construction. If either input is zero, the result is zero; if both are infinity, it is infinity. Compared with [Faris §23.7](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Holder.lean#L57).

Swapping the first two exponents of a Hölder triple preserves its output exponent. The condition is p⁻¹+q⁻¹=r⁻¹, and addition of extended nonnegative values is commutative. This works at zero and infinity as well as for positive finite exponents. No extra assertion about functions or symmetry of a particular analytic operation is involved. Compared with [Faris §23.7](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Holder.lean#L62).

Every extended nonnegative p forms a Hölder triple (p,∞,p), since the reciprocal of infinity is zero. For ordinary exponents this is the relation behind multiplying an Lp function by a bounded function without changing p. The declaration itself records only the exponent equation, and remains valid even at p=0 or p=∞. Compared with [Faris §23.7](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Holder.lean#L65).

Hölder conjugacy is symmetric: if p and q have reciprocals summing to one, then q and p do too. The relation already forces both exponents to be at least one. Endpoint conjugates are exchanged, so (1,∞) becomes (∞,1); symmetry does not require both exponents to be finite. Compared with [Faris §23.7](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Holder.lean#L130).

The exponents two and two are Hölder conjugate because 1/2+1/2=1. This is the exponent pair used in the Cauchy–Schwarz case of Hölder’s inequality. The declaration supplies the arithmetic relation only; it does not itself assert an inequality or introduce an inner product. Both exponents are finite and nonzero. Compared with [Faris §23.7](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Holder.lean#L133).

One and infinity are Hölder conjugate: their extended reciprocals are one and zero, whose sum is one. This includes the standard L1–L∞ endpoint of Hölder’s inequality. The infinity here is an exponent in [0,∞], and its reciprocal is defined to be zero; it is not an ordinary finite real exponent. Compared with [Faris §23.7](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Holder.lean#L139).

Each member of a Hölder-conjugate pair is at least one. The reciprocal-sum equation forces each nonnegative reciprocal to be at most one, and taking reciprocal reverses order. Infinity is permitted and satisfies the conclusion; no separate finiteness assumption is needed. By symmetry, the same bound holds for the other exponent. Compared with [Faris §23.7](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Holder.lean#L144).

A Hölder-conjugate exponent is strictly positive because it is at least one. This statement includes infinity, which is positive in the extended order; it does not imply finiteness. The conjugacy hypothesis is essential: the domain [0,∞] itself contains zero, but zero cannot have a reciprocal contributing to a sum equal to one. Compared with [Faris §23.7](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Holder.lean#L147).

Neither exponent in a Hölder-conjugate pair can be zero. A zero exponent has extended reciprocal infinity, so its sum with any nonnegative reciprocal cannot equal one. The theorem states this for the first exponent; symmetry gives the other. It still allows infinity as an exponent, paired with one. Compared with [Faris §23.7](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Holder.lean#L150).

For a Hölder-conjugate pair, the reciprocals sum to one. This exposes the defining equation with the output exponent already fixed at one. Extended reciprocal makes the endpoint cases exact: (1,∞) gives 1+0=1 and (∞,1) gives 0+1=1. No assumption that both exponents are strictly larger than one is imposed. Compared with [Faris §23.7](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Holder.lean#L152).

For conjugate exponents, 1−p⁻¹ equals q⁻¹. Subtraction in [0,∞] is truncated at zero, but here p⁻¹≤1, so it agrees with ordinary subtraction. The identity also covers p=1,q=∞ and p=∞,q=1, giving zero and one respectively. No additional finiteness hypothesis on p is required. Compared with [Faris §23.7](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Holder.lean#L154).

Within a Hölder-conjugate pair, the first exponent is infinity exactly when the second is one. The reciprocal equation then reads 0+1=1. This identifies the endpoint precisely, rather than merely allowing it. If the first exponent is finite, the second must instead be strictly greater than one, with infinity still possible. Compared with [Faris §23.7](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Holder.lean#L160).

For conjugate exponents with p finite, (p−1)·p⁻¹=q⁻¹, the usual formula (p−1)/p for the conjugate reciprocal. Since conjugacy gives p≥1, truncated subtraction agrees with ordinary subtraction here. Finiteness matters: at p=∞,q=1 the left side becomes ∞·0=0, whereas q⁻¹=1, so the formula would fail. Compared with [Faris §23.7](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Holder.lean#L176).

Reciprocating a quotient gives the reversed quotient, (a/b)⁻¹=b/a, unless both inputs are zero or both are infinity. Either input may individually be an endpoint. The two excluded pairs are necessary: their quotient is zero and hence has reciprocal infinity, while reversing the equal inputs still gives zero under Lean’s conventions. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Inv.lean#L259).

Reciprocal commutes with every natural-number power of an extended nonnegative value. Positive powers exchange the zero and infinity cases under reciprocal. Exponent zero is also included: both zeroth powers are one, even when the base is zero or infinity, and the reciprocal of one is one. No finite or nonzero base restriction is needed. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Inv.lean#L94).

An extended nonnegative reciprocal is at least one exactly when the original value is at most one. The equivalence includes both endpoints: zero has reciprocal infinity, so both conditions hold there; infinity has reciprocal zero, so both fail there. This uses the globally order-reversing extended reciprocal, not an ordinary reciprocal restricted to positive finite inputs. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Inv.lean#L320).

The reciprocal of an extended nonnegative value is at most one exactly when the original value is at least one. Infinity is included: its reciprocal is zero, and both inequalities hold. At zero both fail because its reciprocal is infinity. Thus no separate positivity or finiteness assumptions are needed for the exact equivalence. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Inv.lean#L318).

An extended nonnegative reciprocal is strictly positive exactly when the input is finite. Zero is a permitted input: its reciprocal is infinity, which is positive in this ordered domain. Infinity is the sole excluded input because its reciprocal is zero. Positive output here does not mean that the output itself is finite. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Inv.lean#L280).
